newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev falls to 715-720 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev falls to 715-720 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 715-720 per dollar in early interbank trade from Thursday's close at 698-702 due to higher dollar demand on an illiquid local forex market, dealers said.
"A bank bought $100,000-200,000 at 710-712 levs at soon as the market opened, pressuring the lev in volatile trade," one dealer said. He declined to elaborate.
"An underlying downward trend for the lev makes the market very nervous and the lev weakens with every dollar purchase at a higher level," another dealer said.
The dollar was bid at 710-715 levs and was offered at 725-730 around 1100 local time (0900 GMT). The lev was expected to fall further today if dollar demand does not subside, traders said.
The central bank was not seen supporting the lev through dollar sales. Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Expectations of a further lev decline were based on the shortage of foreign currency in the economy and the continuing political instability in Bulgaria, the second dealer added.

"Export revenues are low low, proceeds from sell-offs are low, no fresh funding from abroad is in sight, Bulgaria has very large foreign debt payments. How could you then expect a stable lev?", a third dealer said.
Bulgaria has to pay some $135 million coupon on Brady bonds at the end of the month out of a total $300 million foreign debt payments due in the first quarter alone.
Central bank foreing exchange reserves stood at $518 million at the end of December.
The ruling Socialist party and the opposition said they were ready to hold talks on early general elections, but no agreement has been reached yet. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
